core_obligations: From one family to the other (proof lines 1413-1434): isomorphisms of the category act as isomorphisms on values of a presheaf, so a compatible family over the first family is transported along the given isomorphisms to a compatible family over the second, and the sheaf condition for the second family produces a unique amalgamation.

Back to the first family (proof lines 1435-1442): for a member of the first family the author produces an isomorphism to a fibre product with a member of the second family and uses the compatibility of the transported sections to conclude that the amalgamation restricts to the original section.
proof_roadmap: Transport compatible families along the isomorphisms supplied by tautological equivalence.
Apply the sheaf condition for one family to obtain a unique amalgamation.
Check that the amalgamation restricts to the given sections for the other family.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that two tautologically equivalent families with a fixed target give the same sheaf condition for every presheaf (statement lines 1398-1410). The proof is a complete argument in one direction, the other being symmetric: a compatible family for one family is transported along the isomorphisms provided by the tautological equivalence to a compatible family for the other (proof lines 1413-1434), the sheaf condition for the latter produces a unique amalgamation, and the author verifies by producing an isomorphism onto a fibre product that the amalgamation restricts to the original sections (proof lines 1435-1442). The non-formal content is the transport of the compatibility conditions along the isomorphisms. The claim is H2: a written-out implication with the symmetry noted.
